response.explanation_markdown:
### Answer

The selected area has satellite thermal detections **consistent with active burning**. They support a possible fire, but satellite hotspots alone do not confirm a wildfire: industrial heat and other burning can also produce detections. [5] Identifying a named incident or its ignition cause requires matching independent reports or a fire perimeter.

### Satellite observations

The local FIRMS archive contains **1,232 satellite detections** in the **Selected area at 40.355°, -4.514°** for **2026-07-24** (Aqua, N20, N21, SNPP, Terra). [5]

### Power measurements

- Summed instantaneous FRP: **56,169.64 MW**.
- Strongest individual detection: **1,509.70 MW**.

This sum is not energy, burned area or the number of fires.

The query uses H3 R7 cells inside a study envelope, not an administrative boundary or a mapped fire perimeter.

citations.title: NASA FIRMS active fire observations
citations.relevance_note: Local accepted, deduplicated detection centers; detections are not distinct fires. FRP is power in MW, not energy or burned area.
